title: Env and profile removal, CLI wiring

details.contract:
app/src/shared/config.ts ends up exporting exactly:

export interface Budgets { defaultTokens: number; maxTokens: number }
export interface AppConfig { dataDir: string; repoRoot: string; cursorKey: string; budgets: Budgets }
export interface LoadConfigOptions { argv?: readonly string[]; env?: Record<string, string | undefined>; cwd?: string }
export function loadConfig(options?: LoadConfigOptions): AppConfig
export function detectRepoRoot(cwd: string): string
export function flagValue(argv: readonly string[], name: string): string | undefined

Delete PROFILES, Profile, isProfile, AppConfig.profile, the AgentToolName-style exports that no longer apply, and every read of CODEGRAPH_REPO_ROOT, CODEGRAPH_DATA_DIR and CODEGRAPH_PROFILE; the only environment read left in this file is CODEGRAPH_CURSOR_KEY (and the injected `env` option stays for tests).

flagValue(argv, name) returns the value of `--<name> value` or `--<name>=value` and undefined when absent. It scans the WHOLE argv it is given, in any position, because the CLI passes `process.argv.slice(2)` with the tool token still in it and the global flags may appear before or after that token.

Resolution: repoRoot = flagValue(argv,'repo-root') resolved against cwd when present, otherwise detectRepoRoot(cwd ?? process.cwd()). dataDir = flagValue(argv,'data-dir') ? resolve(repoRoot, value) : join(repoRoot, '.codegraph').

detectRepoRoot(cwd) walks from resolve(cwd) upward: at each directory return it when join(dir,'.codegraph') exists, else when join(dir,'.git') exists (a file or a directory — linked worktrees use a file); stop after the filesystem root; return resolve(cwd) when nothing matched. Use node:fs existsSync and node:path only; no git subprocess.

This task temporarily breaks the typecheck for app/src/index.ts, app/src/tools/index/manifest.ts and four test files; later tasks in this same phase repair them, so typecheck is expected red here.

details.contract:
app/src/index.ts becomes the CLI composition root, with this exact grammar pinned:

RESERVED VERBS stay bootstrap-capable. `main(mode, argv)` handles `mcp` -> runMcp(config), `worker` -> runWorker(workerOptions(argv, config)) and `index` -> runWorker(workerOptions(argv, config)), exactly as today. `index` is the one name that is both a reserved verb and a registered tool: the verb is the bootstrap and the repair path (today `openStore` returns `absent` on a fresh tree, so a tool call could not create the first index), while the MCP tool of the same name serves clients. Both accept the same arguments (`--force`, `--mode full|fast`). Every other name is looked up in TOOLS and dispatched to `runTool(tool.name, argv.slice(1), config)`.

`cgraph --repo-root X status` is not legal (the verb or tool name must be argv[0]); an unknown name writes `cgraph: unknown tool "<name>"` to stderr and returns EXIT_USAGE; the bin entry prints usage when main returns EXIT_USAGE. `loadConfig({ argv })` still resolves repoRoot/dataDir for every verb because flagValue scans the whole argv.

runTool(name, argv, config): (1) wrap `splitGlobals(argv)` AND `parseCliArgs(...)` in one try/catch for CliUsageError, because splitGlobals can itself refuse a global flag with no value — write error.message and error.usage to stderr and return EXIT_USAGE; (2) when `help`, write `usageOf(name, tool.input)` to stdout and return 0; (3) `openStore(config)`; (4) `refused` writes the error message and hint to stderr and returns EXIT_FAILURE; (5) `absent`: when name === 'status' write `store.reason` to stdout and return 0, otherwise write renderEnvelope of a bootstrapping envelope built with the existing boundarySpec helper and return EXIT_FAILURE; (6) `ready`: call `tool.handle({ ...store.context, log: scopedLog(name) }, args)`, compute `const envelope = route(result, name, store.staleReason)`, then write `name === 'status' && !json ? statusLines(envelope) : renderEnvelope(envelope)` to stdout, and return exitCodeOf(envelope). A handler throwing is caught, logged and returned as EXIT_FAILURE with the failure envelope printed, mirroring callTool.

Because `status` is a tool name, the `status` case in main's switch and the whole runStatus function are deleted; its human output is reproduced by runTool through statusLines. No dead code may remain.

Registration: RegisteredTool loses `readonly profile`; registerableTools is deleted; runMcp uses the TOOLS array directly (`const byName = new Map(TOOLS.map(...))`) and its mcp.ready log drops the `profile` field.

profile removal is complete, including prose, error strings and imports: the header comment (~line 4), the TOOLS comment (~line 148), the registerableTools comment block (~lines 166-168), the two callTool refusals (`no tool named "x" in this surface` ~line 535, `the tool does not exist in this surface` ~line 545), and the `import ... { type Profile }` line (~line 37) which must be deleted because the type no longer exists.

Imports: `import { type InputField, type InputLiteral, parseArgs, parseCliArgs, usageOf, splitGlobals, CliUsageError } from "#shared/cli/args";` (InputField is still used by itemSchemaOf, propertySchemaOf and inputSchemaOf) and `import { EXIT_FAILURE, EXIT_USAGE, exitCodeOf, renderEnvelope, statusLines } from "#shared/cli/render";`. Delete the local InputField, InputLiteral, ToolArgs, matchesType, matchesItem, expectationOf and parseArgs declarations.

Hints: guardRoot's hint becomes `point --data-dir at this tree's own .codegraph directory`, and the two hints that say `run codegraph index` become `run cgraph index` (~lines 381 and 422).

workerOptions: keep --mode and --force only; repoRoot/dataDir come from the config built by loadConfig({ argv }). Do not change callTool's logic, answer, route, openStore, guardRoot's comparison, the watcher startup condition or the MCP request handlers, beyond the profile removals named above. Do not create a new file.

app/src/shared/instructions.ts, its byte-identical copy app/docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md and app/tests/instructions.test.ts move from two surfaces to one. app/tests/instructions.test.ts is the only test file this task owns: the three process-level suites that also import the removed constants are migrated by TASK-013, TASK-014 and TASK-015, so do not edit them and do not run a whole-project typecheck here.

Constants: delete `ADMIN_TOOL_NAMES`, `AGENT_TOOL_NAMES` and `AgentToolName`; keep `TOOL_NAMES` with all seven names in today's order and keep `export type ToolName`. `NEXT_TOOLS` becomes `Readonly<Record<ToolName, readonly ToolName[]>>` with the same values as today (status: summary/search; summary: impact/trace/expand; trace: expand; search: trace/expand; impact: trace/expand; expand: trace; index: status). `nextToolsFor` keeps returning a fresh array and an empty array for an unknown name.

Text of the guide: the title line (~line 74) becomes `# Using the graph: five rules, seven tools, one bound repository`; the module doc comment (~line 2, "with six tools") and the two routing comments (~lines 13, 40) stop referring to a profile; the closing sentence (~line 132, "The agent profile has exactly six tools: …") is replaced by a paragraph naming all seven tools and stating, in these words or equally explicit: call `index` only when `status` says the graph is broken, and never as a query — a rebuild is a repair. Delete the first `## Do not` bullet ("Do not call `index`.") so three anti-patterns remain. Every other heading, rule, example and anti-pattern bullet stays as it is.

Doc copy: app/docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md must stay byte-identical to INSTRUCTIONS_TEXT; apply the same edits there.

Tests: replace AGENT_TOOL_NAMES/ADMIN_TOOL_NAMES usage with TOOL_NAMES throughout; reword the describe/test names and the comment at ~lines 71, 77 and 83 so no test name or comment claims a profile (for example `instructions: nextToolsFor routes within the surface`); the test that checked "the agent profile is described as exactly six tools" becomes a check that the guide names all seven; the test that required the string `do not call \`index\`` becomes a check for the repair-rule wording; the anti-pattern list drops the index entry and keeps three; the routing test asserts every suggestion is in TOOL_NAMES and never the tool itself. Keep the heading-order test passing (no new heading was added).
details.goal: The one-screen guide describes seven tools, turns the old hard exclusion of index into an instruction about when it is appropriate, and no longer mentions a profile anywhere in code or test names.
steps: Edit the constants, NEXT_TOOLS types and doc comments in instructions.ts, and delete the AgentToolName type.
Rewrite the guide title, delete the index anti-pattern bullet and replace the closing six-tool sentence with the seven-tool paragraph.
Mirror the same edits into app/docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md.
Update tests/instructions.test.ts: new exports, reworded describe/test names and comment, new wording checks, keeping the byte-identity test between constant and doc.
Run the file and the profile grep.
details.verify:
cd app && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test tests/instructions.test.ts && ! grep -n "AGENT_TOOL_NAMES\|ADMIN_TOOL_NAMES\|AgentToolName\|profile" src/shared/instructions.ts tests/instructions.test.ts docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md
Done when: the file passes, the doc copy test still compares the two copies, and the grep prints nothing.

tasks.title: Rewrite the instructions guide for one seven-tool surface

details.contract:
Read-only gate over the integrated phase_1 result. Do not edit source or tests; report defects with file and line instead. The phase's owned paths are app/src/shared/config.ts, app/src/shared/instructions.ts, app/src/index.ts, app/bin/codegraph.ts, app/src/indexer/watch.ts, app/src/tools/*/manifest.ts, app/src/tools/index/handler.ts, app/docs/INSTRUCTIONS.md and the migrated files under app/tests/. app/package.json was owned by phase_0 and must not have changed again.

Checks: typecheck, lint, the whole suite (binary-smoke includes a compiled build), then two production-side sweeps. Tests are allowed to name the removed identifiers as negative assertions; production code and user-facing docs are not. Sweep A: grep -rn "CODEGRAPH_REPO_ROOT\|CODEGRAPH_DATA_DIR\|CODEGRAPH_PROFILE" over app/src app/bin app/docs app/README.md must be empty. Sweep B: grep -rn "profile" over app/src app/bin app/docs must be empty.

Then a manual smoke in a throwaway tree: mktemp -d, two small source files, then `$HOME/.bun/bin/bun run /ABSOLUTE/PATH/TO/app/bin/codegraph.ts index` with cwd inside the temp tree (the entry path must be absolute — a relative entry cannot resolve from another cwd); assert it exits 0 and creates .codegraph/graph.db. From a nested subdirectory with no CODEGRAPH_* variable set, run status, status --json, search, trace, impact, and record each command with its exit code.

Expected: index exits 0 and creates the database; `status` prints five human lines and exits 0; `status --json` prints one JSON envelope and exits 0; search/trace/impact print one JSON envelope each and exit 0; `cgraph nonsense` and `cgraph trace` exit 2.
details.goal: Prove the breaking phase left one surface, zero removed variables outside tests, a working bootstrap and a working CLI.
steps: Run typecheck and lint.
Run the full test suite and record pass/fail counts and any file that failed.
Run the two production-side sweeps and report their output verbatim.
Bootstrap a temp tree with an absolute entry path, then run the query commands from a nested directory and report each with its exit code.
List any file in the diff that no phase_1 task owns.
details.verify:
cd app && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run typecheck && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun run lint && $HOME/.bun/bin/bun test && ! grep -rn "CODEGRAPH_REPO_ROOT\|CODEGRAPH_DATA_DIR\|CODEGRAPH_PROFILE" src bin docs README.md && ! grep -rn "profile" src bin docs
Done when: typecheck and lint are clean, the suite is green, both sweeps print nothing, index bootstrapped a fresh tree, and status (five lines), status --json, search, trace and impact all exited 0 from a nested directory.
